title: How Billables AI Software Helps Law Firms Price Flat Fees
summary: A fixed price gives the client cost certainty, but the firm still needs an accurate record of the work required. Captured effort data helps firms price the next matter and measure the margin on the last one.
body_markdown:
### AI Summary


-


A flat fee is one agreed set price for a legal job, agreed before the work starts.


-


The client pays the same amount however long the job takes. The firm still pays for every hour its lawyers work.


-


To price the next similar job at a profit, the firm needs to know how many hours the last one took.


-


Billables AI software records billable work as it happens.


## What is a Flat Fee?


A flat fee is a fixed price for a defined piece of legal work, such as drafting a contract or filing a trademark. The client knows the cost up front. If the work takes longer than planned, the firm absorbs the extra cost.


Flat fees are one type of alternative fee arrangement (AFA), which is a[fee arrangement based on factors other than hourly rates alone](https://www.iadclaw.org/assets/1/7/4.1-_NY_State_Bar_Journal_May_2012_Ethical_Issues_And_Alternative_Fee_Arrangements.pdf) , customized to the particular client and matter.


## Why Does a Flat Fee Still Need a Time Record?


Pricing the next flat fee and calculating the margin on the completed matter both depend on how long the work actually took.


The client may see one agreed price, but the firm still incurs effort across partners, associates, and other professionals. That effort is part of the firm’s cost of delivering the matter. If the internal record understates it, the matter can appear healthier than it was, which encourages the firm to repeat an unprofitable price.


The record generally comes from work captured as it happens or hours[reconstructed from memory after the fact](https://pointone.com/blog/how-law-firms-lose-revenue-to-manual-timekeeping) . Billables AI tools capture work as it happens, so attorneys never have to reconstruct their day.


## How Should a Firm Price its Next Flat Fee?


Price the next flat fee against the effort the last comparable matter actually required, rather than simply repeating the number that won the work.


The starting point is a group of matters with genuinely comparable scope. A routine filing should not set the benchmark for an engagement requiring negotiation, unfamiliar issues, or sustained partner judgment. The distinction matters when[pricing commoditized work differently from work that needs partner judgment](https://pointone.com/attorneyintelligence/ai-economics-pricing/) .


The firm can then examine effort by matter type, work phase, and timekeeper. If previous matters repeatedly required more senior attention than expected, the next quote should reflect that delivery model. If associates handled most of the work within a stable process, the firm may have more room to offer a predictable fee.


Before the engagement is signed, the proposed fee should be compared with the likely effort cost. Pricing below that cost turns the matter type into a recurring loss. Correcting the next quote protects revenue by giving the firm a price capable of covering the resources the work usually consumes.


This requires visibility into[margin per matter](https://pointone.com/blog/law-firm-financial-reporting) , not just the fee collected from the client. Around 75% of partners in[LawVision’s 2025 Strategic Pricing Law Firm Survey](https://lawvision.com/navigating-pricing-in-an-uncertain-legal-economy-lessons-from-the-2025-strategic-pricing-law-firm-survey/) said they did not know their fair value, and 54% said they did not understand the relationship between pricing and profitability. That uncertainty makes it difficult to set a defensible fixed fee because the decision lacks a reliable connection to delivery cost.


## How Does Billables AI Turn Captured Work Into Pricing Data?


Billables AI is AI software that records billable work as it happens and turns it into time entries. An AI-native billables system does three things:


-


**Captures work** from the tools lawyers already use, such as email, documents, calls, and calendars.


-


**Drafts time entries** from that work, each assigned to a client and a matter.


-


**Turns hours into data** the firm can use to price work, plan staffing, and measure profit.


PointOne is a billables AI platform built on this approach: it captures work as it happens and generates compliant, bill-ready time entries. **PointOne**[captures attorney work automatically](https://pointone.com/blog/law-firm-ai-time-capture) across email, documents, calls and meetings, then drafts time entries for attorneys to review and send straight to the firm's billing system.


The approved record can then show how effort was distributed across matters and matter types.[PointOne Intelligence](https://pointone.com/product/intelligence) analyzes captured time data to identify work patterns, bottlenecks, and inefficiencies, provide visibility into staffing and resource allocation, and support more accurate pricing estimates and margin analysis for flat-fee pricing. For example, the firm can see whether a supposedly repeatable engagement consistently absorbs unexpected partner attention, whether staffing assumptions match delivery, and whether the fee leaves an acceptable margin.


## Transparent Flat Fees Start With Better Time Data


There is still limited visibility into how flat fees are price to the client. AI platforms for billables, like PointOne, provide law firms with the time data to break down what the work cost and increase transparency with clients.

## FAQs


What is billables AI?


Billables AI is AI software that captures billable work as it happens, drafts time entries from it, and turns those hours into data for pricing and profit analysis.


What happens if a flat fee matter takes longer than expected?


The firm absorbs the extra cost. The client still pays the agreed price, so every additional hour reduces the firm’s margin on that matter. Tracking time internally shows how much the overrun cost and whether the next quote for similar work should change.


What types of legal work are best suited for flat fees?


Legal work with a defined scope and repeatable process, such as drafting a standard contract or filing a trademark application, is easier to price at a fixed fee. More unpredictable work, such as complex litigation, is harder to price because new evidence, unexpected motions, and changing circumstances can significantly affect the time and expertise required.
